page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the c4a server family. It is powered by an arm64 CPU architecture and features 16 dedicated virtual central processing units (vCPUs) paired with 64.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a balanced resource density of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU core.

This instance type does not include bundled local storage or integrated graphics processing units (GPUs). Network configurations do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing capabilities without resource sharing or burstable performance degradation.

The c4a-standard-16 is designed for general-purpose workloads that benefit from the power efficiency and architecture of arm64 processors. Suitable deployment scenarios include application servers, containerized microservices, web serving, and software development environments. The hardware profile offers a balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio, providing resource density suitable for multi-threaded applications that do not require specialized hardware accelerators or local NVMe storage.
